narrative:
The model estimates a 75% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors about your professional situation.

The strongest influence is that you have received other job opportunities while at your company. Having external offers is a major signal that you may be considering leaving, and this factor pushed the prediction most strongly toward departure.

Your total years of experience across all jobs came next. With 6-10 years of overall experience—higher than the majority of employees the model expects to stay—this also increased the likelihood of leaving, as more seasoned professionals often explore new paths.

In contrast, your 6-10 years spent specifically in this organization worked in the other direction, modestly pulling the prediction toward staying. It suggests you have built some roots here, though not enough to outweigh the other signals.

The organization should consider discussing your external opportunities with you openly and exploring whether stronger retention measures, such as clearer promotion paths or enhanced recognition, could align with your career goals. You, in turn, may want to reflect on what would make staying fulfilling before making any decisions. (218 words)
